implementation_notes: The Swift server-side realization is a Vapor route closure whose transaction boundary comes from Fluent: req.db.transaction { database in ... } opens a transaction on the request's database, commits when the closure returns and rolls back if it throws, and every statement inside must use the supplied database handle instead of req.db. The script itself is a straight line of model queries, written either with async/await or by chaining EventLoopFutures. Swift's type/struct layering is not needed for the pattern, which is why this counts as framework-provided rather than hand-written; explicit transaction control remains available for scripts that talk to several databases or need custom isolation.
pitfalls: Using req.db instead of the closure's database handle inside the transaction runs statements outside it.
Only errors thrown inside the closure roll back; a failure after the transaction returned cannot undo it - keep fallible work inside.
The closure's database is pinned to one connection, so awaiting slow external work inside it holds the transaction open and can exhaust the pool.
